title: Comeback atlas: where the model nails the game state
headline_insight: For a 1-to-5 point lead with 24-36 minutes left, the model's mean win probability is 0.6204 across 898 games and teams in that state actually won 62.03% of the time -- a near-perfect calibration match.
what_it_means: The reliability map is reshaped into a lead-by-time-remaining atlas of 84 game-state buckets, each carrying the model's win probability, the in-play market price, and the realized outcome frequency. In the bulk of regulation states the model tracks reality closely, like the 1-5 point early lead above. The honest exception is overtime: with a 1-5 lead in OT the model says 0.7113 while teams actually won 98.3% and the market priced 97.6% -- the model under-rates how decisive a late lead is, and the market is better there.
how_to_read: Each cell compares model_mean_prob, market_mean_prob, and outcome_rate for a bucket; buckets with fewer than 30 games are masked from the headline but still listed.
why_it_matters: It is a pure calibration exhibit -- model versus market versus what really happened, by game state -- showing both where the forecaster is trustworthy and exactly where it still trails the market.
caveat: Calibration/reliability measurement only, never a $/ROI/edge claim. Buckets below 30 games are masked; the widest gaps sit in thin overtime cells.
